Bitcoin and space travel are two of the fastest-growing areas of venture-capital funding
And we all know that this is because of Voat! Go Goats!

I'm not sure how to feel about this. I'll be commenting on space travel by the way.

Initially I see lots of people having a positive view of this. More money for space travel -> more research into it and more developement -> more breakthroughs and advances in propulsion and habitat technologies -> yay star trek future.

But I don't think people will see the negative side. And it's a big one. People invest to see a return. The fact that VC is funding space travel, and not some other non-investy way, means that space travel will be fueled by profit.

This could end up turning space travel into just another shop.

Oh and if VC gets big in space travel, the entire thing will explode in patents, like everything investy goes to.

This is just really, really terrible news, in disguise I think.

The public funding approach (NASA) has been tried and frankly its been a failure. Sure discoveries and some science has been made but no large scale attemps at moving people to space has made it passed the drawing board. Historically the only model we know of sustained expansion and colonization has been based on exploitation and capital. It's ugly, at times unethical, genocidal even, but we know it works.

In order to truly conquer space we need to develop a sustainable economy up there. No way around that.

Yes but what I was commenting on was VC, not businesses setting up.

More space businesses would be fantastic

It's businesses with investors, i.e. VC-funded businesses.

That is the truly depressing part.

Space, if anything to humans, will just be the next Candy-Crush, with rockets. And that saddens me.

The public funding approach (NASA) has been tried and frankly its been a failure. Sure discoveries and some science has been made but no large scale attemps at moving people to space has made it passed the drawing board.

What? How so? Landing on the moon, Mars Rovers, pictures of Pluto, ISS, and all the technology that came from it. How do you call this a failure?

As an attempt to open a new frontier in space, that's how. There's no permanent economically viable presence outside of LEO. No moon base, no asteroid mines, no large scale space based industries. There are no people making their lives (living, breathing, dying) in space. You have to read my comment in the context of the parent's comment.
